author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.
decisions:

  the way the project records non-goal changes.

The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correcting a booked visit
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected afterwards. The correction replaces what was recorded on that visit rather than adding a second visit to the pet, and is held to the same rules as booking.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction of a booked visit shows that visit's recorded date and description, ready to be changed.
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that visit's details and shows the owner's record.
A pet with one booked visit still has exactly one visit after a correction to it succeeds.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
A date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
An owner's record offers no way to correct a visit.
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, narrowed but not retired)
an entry point to the correction from the owner's record, or from any other page
changing which pet a visit belongs to
refusing a correction that names a visit not belonging to the named pet: unstated in the intake, recorded as an open question
notes: Owner-stated boundary constraints, quoted from the intake-decision at line 1: the correction is reached at 'GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit' with POST to the same URL; it reuses 'the existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit` model attribute'. These are the owner's, not design proposals; the design stage owns everything else about mechanism. Three open questions are recorded in docs/prd.md Open Questions and none blocks this slice: the missing entry point, the mismatched-pet case, and whether a correction shows the pet's other visits (REQ-VIS-002 binds booking only). Out of my write scope: docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-correction-admitted.md.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The correction reuses the create-or-update form-controller shape PetController already realizes, now recorded in docs/system-design.md as the Create-or-update form controllers subsection: one @ModelAttribute loader serves both /new and /{id}/edit, takes the identifier as an optional path variable, and resolves the child by navigating from the Owner aggregate root. No new controller, module, template, repository, or dependency; no ADR beyond the non-goal ADR already written. The one adjustment is that VisitController.loadPetWithVisit unconditionally constructs a Visit and attaches it to the Pet, which the correction path must not do; the loader becomes visitId-aware and attaches nothing when a visitId is present. Grep-resolved (no IDE oracle connected in this run), so the weaker basis: VisitController.java:63-93 and PetController.java:75-87 read directly.
integration_points: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit takes visitId as an optional path variable, mirroring PetController.findPet. Absent leaves booking unchanged; present returns the pet's existing visit and attaches nothing to the pet.
Pet gains getVisit(Integer id), mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id), so the controller stays out of the visits collection.
GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit are added to VisitController. The class-level @InitBinder and the minVisitDate model attribute cover them unchanged.
The correction POST binds the form onto the Visit the loader resolved from the graph, then calls owners.save(owner); the Owner-Pet-Visit cascade issues an update rather than an insert.
An unresolvable visitId throws IllegalArgumentException naming the id, matching the pet-not-found branch already in loadPetWithVisit.
createOrUpdateVisitForm.html needs no edit: it carries no action attribute and posts back to the URL that served it, and ${visit['new']} is already false for a persisted visit.
The success path redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId}, which resolves from the correction URL unchanged.

patterns.description: the create-or-update loader: one @ModelAttribute method with an optional identifier path variable serving both /pets/new and /pets/{petId}/edit
Owner.getPet(Integer) - the by-identifier lookup on the aggregate that Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors
the shape this triage recorded in durable memory, including the rule that a nested entity is reached only by navigating from the owner
@WebMvcTest(VisitController.class) with a mocked OwnerRepository returning a real Owner graph; the pet's visit count is asserted against that graph

risks.risk: loadPetWithVisit unconditionally constructs a Visit and calls pet.addVisit. Left unguarded on the correction path, the pet gains a second visit and acceptance criterion 3 fails.
risks.mitigation: The visitId branch attaches nothing; the correction binds onto the visit already in the graph.

risks.risk: Binding a fresh Visit instance instead of the resolved one inserts a row rather than updating it: Pet.visits is a LinkedHashSet and BaseEntity does not override equals, so a second instance is a second element.
risks.mitigation: Bind onto the loader's return value; add no element to pet.visits on the correction path.

risks.risk: Copying the non-future-date check into the correction handler puts a second copy of a business rule in a web controller. architecture-principles Pattern Catalog states a new rule in a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the recorded deviation.
risks.mitigation: Extract the existing check into one private method both POST handlers call. The rule count stays at one; no new rule is added.

risks.risk: Reaching for a VisitValidator wired with dataBinder.setValidator, as PetController does for pets, would replace bean validation and silently drop @NotBlank on description, regressing REQ-VIS-001's blank-description refusal.
risks.mitigation: Keep @Valid and the existing binder untouched. Moving the visit-date rule out of the controller belongs to system-design.md Open Questions item 2, not to this slice.

risks.risk: Form binding mutates the loaded Visit before validation runs, so a refused correction leaves a dirty in-memory entity while the acceptance criteria require the visit to keep its recorded details.
risks.mitigation: The Owner is detached (spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled) and the refusal path never calls save, so nothing reaches the database. The two refusal tests assert the repository is never saved.

risks.risk: Three path identifiers with no authentication (NG-1) invite reaching a visit through a pet that does not own it.
risks.mitigation: Resolution navigates owner to pet to visit, so a visit outside the named pet is structurally unreachable and the request fails closed. Introduce no VisitRepository and no lookup by visit identifier alone.

notes:
Autofix audit: the log holds no design-doc-autofix records; nothing to judge.

The product expert's open question - whether a correction should refuse a visitId not belonging to the named pet - does need a design answer, and the answer is a mechanism constraint rather than a product rule. Because the visit is resolved by navigating Owner to Pet to Visit, a visitId outside the named pet has nothing to return, and the loader throws the same IllegalArgumentException its pet-not-found branch already throws. The refusal therefore falls out of the resolution strategy and needs no requirement. The PRD's open question - whether a stated, tested refusal behaviour is wanted, with a friendlier response than the error page - stays open and does not block this slice. No requirement is added and no acceptance criterion changes.

Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/system-design.md gains the Create-or-update form controllers subsection under Contracts, describing state read off PetController today rather than the slice's future state; docs/adr/README.md gains the index row for 2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-correction-admitted.md, which the product expert flagged as outside its write scope. No new ADR: extending VisitController rather than adding a second controller follows the existing precedent, departs from no pattern, and is cheap to reverse.

Deferred to doc-sync after the code lands: the Contracts table rows for VisitController, Visit, Pet, and OwnerRepository gain REQ-VISITEDIT-001 in Implements, and the VisitController purpose line gains correction alongside booking.

Guidance on choices the acceptance criteria leave silent, both narrowest-reading: add no flash message, since REQ-VISITEDIT-001 asks only that the owner's record be shown and the existing hard-coded confirmations are a standing REQ-LANG-002 deviation not worth extending; and leave the submit button's #{addVisit} key alone, since a correction-specific label needs a new key in all eleven locale bundles under REQ-LANG-002 and widens the slice past its criteria. The prd-entry lists createOrUpdateVisitForm.html as a file target; this design expects zero edits to it, and the template's previous-visits table already renders for a persisted visit, which settles the third PRD open question by existing behaviour.

security-principles rows checked against the slice. Mass assignment: the class-level @InitBinder disallowing id and *.id already covers the new handlers - do not narrow it to a named attribute. Trusting cross-request state: the loader re-resolves owner, pet, and visit on the POST, so nothing is carried over from the GET. Widening the exposed surface: two new routes, unauthenticated like every other route under NG-1, mutating a visit the same caller can already create; the ADR records that the capability is reachable by its URL alone. Secret disclosure through errors: the not-found message carries only path identifiers, which matters because the error page renders exception messages (Known Defects).

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Owner binding on the new POST is inherited, not introduced, but worth recording: processVisitCorrectionForm takes @ModelAttribute Owner owner (VisitController:136) and then calls owners.save(owner). Spring applies request-parameter binding to that attribute, Owner.getPets() returns the live list, and the handler carries no @Valid on the owner - so a crafted POST to the correction URL can write owner fields (and indexed pets[n] properties) and persist them unvalidated. This is byte-for-byte the shape of the existing processNewVisitForm, and the same writes are already reachable unauthenticated via /owners/{id}/edit, so it adds no attacker capability and the project's two-question test in docs/security-principles.md 'Applying this section' passes. If it is ever tightened, tighten both handlers together with @ModelAttribute(binding = false) so the pattern stays consistent - a demonstration app's patterns get copied.

No NVD match ran in this review: build.gradle configures no OWASP dependency-check plugin (plugins block lists java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management, native, cyclonedx, javaformat), and the reviewer has no network access. The framework versions are unverified against the NVD; the CycloneDX SBOM task is present and would let CI close the check. The change itself alters no dependency, so this is a standing project gap rather than a slice finding.
approved_aspects: Insecure direct object reference: the correction resolves the visit by navigating Owner -> Pet -> Visit (VisitController.loadPetWithVisit:73-96, Pet.getVisit:92-99, Owner.getPet:117). No VisitRepository and no lookup by visit identifier alone is introduced, so a visitId outside the named pet is structurally unreachable and the request fails closed with IllegalArgumentException rather than silently editing another pet's visit. Grep-resolved reads (no IDE oracle connected in this run) - the weaker basis.

Trusting cross-request state: the POST handler re-resolves owner, pet, and visit through the same @ModelAttribute loader that served the GET. Nothing is carried across requests, and the identifier is re-validated against the graph on every call. Matches the security-principles row of the same name.

Mass assignment: both new handlers sit under the existing class-level @InitBinder setAllowedFields, which disallows 'id' and '*.id' (VisitController:52-55). The security-principles control ('every request-bound type explicitly disallows identifier binding') is satisfied for the new endpoints; the binder was correctly left un-narrowed rather than scoped to one attribute.

Error message disclosure: the new not-found message carries only the two path integers ('Visit with id N not found for pet with id M.'). Both are typed path variables (int / Integer), so no attacker-controlled string reaches it. This matters because the error page renders the exception message (system-design Known Defects), and error.html line 20 renders ${message} with th:text, which escapes - no reflected XSS path.

Cross-site scripting: pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm.html is unchanged and renders every request-derived value through th:text / the escaping input fragment; no th:utext, no th:action, no inline script, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing of request text was introduced.

Widening the exposed surface: two routes added (GET and POST .../visits/{visitId}/edit), unauthenticated like every route under the recorded NG-1 baseline. They mutate a visit the same anonymous caller can already create and edit through /visits/new and /owners/{id}/edit, so no new capability or privilege is reached. The exposure is stated in docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-correction-admitted.md and in the PRD entry.

Injection and unsafe operations: detection-pattern sweep over the two changed production files returns nothing for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, Files/FileWriter/FileOutputStream, enableDefaultTyping/@JsonTypeInfo, java.util.Random, System.out/err, and system /tmp. Data access stays on the Spring Data derived-query repository; no string-concatenated query text, no regex, no file or XML parsing added.

Fail-secure refusal path: a rejected correction never calls owners.save, and spring.jpa.open-in-view=false (application.properties:11) keeps the Owner detached, so binding's in-memory mutation of the loaded Visit cannot flush. Both refusal tests assert the repository is never saved (VisitControllerTests:170,186).

Concurrency: the controller stays stateless - the new VIEWS_VISITS_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FORM constant is a static final String and rejectDateNotInTheFuture holds no state, so the singleton bean gains no unsynchronized mutable field.

Supply chain: the change set touches no build file and adds no dependency (scripts/changeset.sh --name-only lists only docs, two production classes, and one test class), so no new artifact enters the resolved set.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correcting a booked visit
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected afterwards. The correction replaces what was recorded on that visit rather than adding a second visit to the pet, and is held to the same rules as booking.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the correction of a booked visit shows that visit's recorded date and description, ready to be changed.
Submitting a description and a date later than today updates that visit's details and shows the owner's record.
A pet with one booked visit still has exactly one visit after a correction to it succeeds.
A blank description is refused, the description is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
A date of today or earlier is refused, the date is named, and the visit keeps its recorded details.
An owner's record offers no way to correct a visit.
non_goals: cancelling a booked visit (NG-5, narrowed but not retired)
an entry point to the correction from the owner's record, or from any other page
changing which pet a visit belongs to
refusing a correction that names a visit not belonging to the named pet: unstated in the intake, recorded as an open question

summary: admit correction of a booked visit

blast_radius.note: One module, eight files, no sensitive paths; the only shared surface is VisitController.loadPetWithVisit, which every route in that controller runs, and the booking branch is preserved verbatim behind a visitId == null guard that the existing booking tests still exercise.

semantic_surprise.note: Read every prod hunk and the subtleties resolve: spring.jpa.open-in-view=false means the visit mutated by binding on a refused correction is detached and discarded, save(owner) merges a visit that still carries its id so it updates in place, the isNew guard in Pet.getVisit keeps a transient visit from matching, and an unowned visitId fails closed because resolution navigates owner to pet to visit; the one residual is presentational, the reused template still labels the submit button Add Visit and lists the visit under Previous Visits, which the intake mandated by requiring template reuse.

test_adequacy.note: The tests assert real outcomes on the real objects, not the implementation: they check the recorded Visit instance carries the corrected date and description after the POST, that pet.getVisits() containsExactly that same instance, and that owners.save is never called on either refusal path, plus the not-my-pet guard for both GET and POST; a broken in-place update that appended a second visit would fail two of them.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four dispatched reviewers approved with empty findings in round 2, but two parked recommendations rather than clearing cleanly: security records that no OWASP dependency-check or NVD match has run in any round so supply chain is still unverified by a human or CI, and notes the not-my-pet guard surfaces as a 500 rather than a 404; code-quality parks a loadPetWithVisit Javadoc missing the ownerId and model param tags.

scope_deviation.note: The diff matches the intake decision point by point, both routes, template and model-attribute reuse, in-place update, no owner-detail entry point, NG-5 narrowed through a non-goal ADR, and the three genuinely open choices recorded as PRD open questions instead of answered; the row build_retries 0 and design_revisions 1 understate the log, which holds two round-1 build failures and three design-block records, but the two re-issues corrected path coverage and doc-table coherence and the design itself never moved.

rationale: The code is a faithful mirror of PetController existing create-or-update loader and I could not surprise it by reading. What deserves your minute is the two parked reviewer recommendations: no dependency vulnerability scan has ever run against this tree, and the unowned-visit guard returns a 500.
